issues.description: The solution implementation defines the pixel-setting routine with the label ".set_pixel" (leading dot), while the template and problem statement refer to and call the routine as "set_pixel". This name mismatch between the solution symbol and the expected symbol in the template/main can prevent the call from resolving or confuse students about the correct symbol name to implement.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the routine name consistent: in the solution rename the label to exactly "set_pixel:" (remove the leading dot) so it matches the template and the call sites, or alternatively change the call sites in the template to call the exact symbol defined in the solution. Ensure the symbol name used in the problem statement, template, and solution is identical.

issues.description: The subroutine name for the pixel-writing routine is inconsistent: the problem statement and the template declare/use the symbol 'set_pixel', while the reference solution defines the label '.set_pixel' (leading dot). This difference in identifier naming for the same conceptual entity (the set_pixel subroutine) can confuse students when mapping the problem requirements to the template and the provided solution and may lead to broken calls or difficulty locating the implementation.
issues.suggestedFix: Use a single consistent symbol name for the subroutine across all artifacts. Rename the solution label from '.set_pixel' to 'set_pixel' (or, alternatively, rename the template and problem references to '.set_pixel') so the problem statement, template, and solution all use the exact same identifier.
